commit c3a3d1c48adcf492696029fa946d606e5e7ba40a
Update conn state to prevent concurrent connection attempts

commit 6214c9dd1cd421727852b03cafceac7c9e9eb973
Make callers of resetBackoff() lock the mutex

commit ff977b39fc525a077d16427fad00949e179dc17b
Add doc comment for resetTransportAndUnlock

commit 76ef33f44a600c3ed1a385979fd1dfbcade3fbb6
Merge remote-tracking branch 'source/master' into fix_conn_connect_race

summary.intent: Hold ac.mu across the addrConn's Idle->Connecting transition by having connect() and updateAddrs() keep the lock and hand it to the renamed resetTransportAndUnlock(), instead of releasing it and letting resetTransport() re-acquire it, closing the window where two goroutines could both observe Idle and start concurrent connection attempts (grpc-go#7365).
summary.issue_fit: Met — the supplied PR/issue packet's root-cause analysis (two goroutines both seeing addrConn Idle before either sets Connecting) is closed: connect() and updateAddrs() now hold ac.mu continuously from the Idle check through resetTransportAndUnlock()'s state transition to Connecting, and the doc comment on resetTransportAndUnlock codifies the new locking contract.
summary.coverage: The sole changed file, clientconn.go (+6/-7), was read in full at both merge-base and head, along with its only two call sites of the renamed method (balancer_wrapper.go) and tearDown()/onClose() for interaction with the changed lock discipline. No test files changed in this diff.
check_details: Reviewer ran `go build .` offline at head 76ef33f44a600c3ed1a385979fd1dfbcade3fbb6: succeeded, no errors.

Reviewer ran `go test -race -v -timeout 260s .` offline at the same head: 152 subtests, 0 failures, including TestUpdateAddresses_NoopIfCalledWithSameAddresses, TestResetConnectBackoff, TestBackoffCancel and TestDial_OneBackoffPerRetryGroup, which exercise the changed connect/updateAddrs/resetTransportAndUnlock paths.

observations.fact: Removing the explicit ac.mu.Unlock() in updateAddrs before its deferred ac.transport.GracefulClose() means that deferred call (when ac.transport != nil) now blocks until the spawned `go ac.resetTransportAndUnlock()` goroutine reaches its own unlock, serializing the old transport's close against the new Connecting-state transition instead of letting them race; the full -race suite passed with no hang, so this is a behavior tightening, not a defect.

Commit 6214c9dd1's message, "Make callers of resetBackoff() lock the mutex," misdescribes its own diff, which touches connect(), updateAddrs() and resetTransport()/resetTransportAndUnlock(), not resetBackoff().
observations.evidence: git show 6214c9dd1cd421727852b03cafceac7c9e9eb973 (commit message vs. diff body).

requirements.source: spec-pr7390-packet/pr-body/"This change ensures that caller of resetTransport() keep holding the mutex instead of releasing it and having resetTransport() re-acquire it."
requirements.evidence: clientconn.go:905-923 (connect) and clientconn.go:940-996 (updateAddrs) now call resetTransportAndUnlock while still holding ac.mu, with no intervening Unlock/Lock; the new doc comment at clientconn.go:1231-1233 states "ac.mu must be held by the caller, and this function will guarantee it is released."

requirements.source: spec-pr7390-packet/pr-body/"This ensures that no concurrent requests are able to start once caller of resetTransport does some validation and calls resetTransport."
requirements.evidence: connect() (clientconn.go:906-922) holds ac.mu from the Idle check through resetTransportAndUnlock()'s ac.updateConnectivityState(Connecting) at clientconn.go:1261, so a second concurrent connect()/updateAddrs() call blocks on ac.mu until state has already left Idle, closing the two-tryAllAddrs race described in the packet's issue-7365 root-cause comment; corroborated by the passing -race package suite.

requirements.source: spec-pr7390-packet/release-notes/"client: fix race that could lead to orphaned connections and associated resources."
requirements.evidence: The packet's own root-cause comment reports that the pre-fix race let two resetTransport invocations run concurrently, each creating a transport but only one being recorded in ac.transport, orphaning the other; serializing entry into resetTransportAndUnlock via the held lock prevents the double invocation that caused the orphaning.

requirements.source: spec-pr7390-packet/pr-body/"## Tested Verified that Test/AuthorityRevive no longer flakes for 100000 attempts with the change."
requirements.evidence: A 100000-iteration flake run of xds/internal/xdsclient/tests.Test/AuthorityRevive exceeds the sandbox's 5-minute-per-command, offline execution allowance and that test's full dependency surface is outside this review's scope; the reviewer instead verified the underlying locking mechanism by code inspection and ran the root package's full -race suite (152 subtests, 0 failures) at head, which corroborates but does not reproduce the specific flake-rate claim. Nothing in the merge decision turns on the exact iteration count, since the mechanism itself is independently verified.

requirements.source: spec-pr7390-packet/review-thread-10/"Please add a short comment here: // resetTransportAndUnlock unconditionally connects the addrConn. // ac.mu must be held by the caller, and this function will guarantee it is released."
requirements.evidence: clientconn.go:1231-1233 carries the requested doc comment, added in commit ff977b39f ("Add doc comment for resetTransportAndUnlock").
